requirements.text: BOUNDED-NEGATIVE EVIDENCE DISCIPLINE (correction 1) - Never present a bounded search's negative result as a universal negative. The defensible finding is 'not located in the sources examined' (named), never 'the city never documented it anywhere' or 'further research cannot uncover it'. Applies to all research reports, queue stamps, owner summaries, and provenance notes. Existing overclaims of this shape are corrected when touched (see R006).
requirements.required_harness: research/report review checks negative claims are bounded to named sources
requirements.required_evidence: corrected queue/report wording; reviewer checks on future research tasks citing D-051

requirements.text: UNKNOWN STAYS UNKNOWN (correction 2, part a) - An unknown or ambiguous street width retains the factual status UNKNOWN: the original source text, typed ambiguity class, source/version, and review flag are preserved end-to-end and never presented as a factually verified narrow (or wide) street. A parsed scalar, an interval, an approximation, an unknown, and a zoning conclusion are distinct pieces of information and stay distinct. (The accepted M4-T015 classifier already conforms: it emits narrow_fail_closed + class + review flag, preserving the raw text - this row binds every FUTURE consumer and presentation surface.)
requirements.required_harness: consumer/UI/report tests prove unknown-width inputs surface as unknown-with-review-label, never as verified narrow
requirements.required_evidence: accepted tasks citing D-051-R002 with such tests

requirements.text: PER-RULE CONSERVATIVE-FALLBACK VALIDATION (correction 2, part b) - Any conservative fallback (including fail-closed-to-narrow) must be validated separately for EACH rule that consumes it; the conservative direction differs by rule. Owner's counterexample: ZR 23-433 setback (15 ft narrow vs 10 ft wide - narrow assumption is the stricter envelope) vs ZR 23-431 street-wall placement (70% within 8 ft on wide vs 10 ft on narrow - a narrow assumption could permit placement that FAILS the actual wide-street requirement). A smaller floor-area estimate does not automatically make a generated shape or compliance result safe. Until a fallback is validated for a given consuming rule, that rule's affected results retain their assumption or review label. The one currently-validated case is the accepted r6_r7_r8 wide-street conditional FAR rule (wide only ever raises FAR).
requirements.required_harness: every A2/geometry rule packet consuming street-width classification carries a per-rule conservative-direction analysis + tests proving the fallback direction, or keeps assumption/review labels
requirements.required_evidence: accepted rule tasks citing D-051-R003 with per-rule validation sections in their gate evidence

Fold its confirmed findings into RQ-005 (mapped-width product-level support; sidewalks 'usually' included; feet as intended display units; field definition absent across 14 metadata-authoring versions; value profile 54,051 records / 6,908 non-plain-numeric with exact class counts; ambiguous values on Mapped_St City_St records; DEP property-line-vs-curb-line survey distinction; DOB mapped-street-boundary caution). RQ-005(1) residual stays OPEN, refined to: measurement boundaries, variable-width representation, and encoding conventions. Closure evidence = DCP written specification (dataset contact DCPOpendata@planning.nyc.gov; owner-side outreach) and/or per-record adopted Section/Alteration Map resolution. RQ-005(2) and (3) remain answered.
requirements.required_harness: queue reflects the fold + refined residual; archived report carries the discovery-aid banner

requirements.text: PROPOSED CLASSIFICATION POLICY = INTERPRETATION INPUT ONLY - The researcher's recommended DRAFT width-classification table (clear <75 narrow / clear >=75 wide / explicit bound like >75 possibly wide under a documented owner-approved reading / ambiguous classes resolve-from-map with uncertainty preserved) is INPUT to the OQ-3 ambiguity-class interpretation process (docs/ARCHITECT_REVIEW_QUESTIONS.md, D-048 routing, G6-class ruling). It is never adopted by an implementation task on its own authority; the 75-ft test's express exceptions (12-10 alternate-width and named-street provisions, amended 3/26/2026) are checked separately whenever it is applied.
